# Independent audit of the optimized capacity-law centroid obstruction

Audited `candidate d26e9d073c9268ac` in full.
The result passes without a required correction.

* The triangle B has area one. With s=sqrt(2)/10, A=sB has area 1/50
  and is contained in B. The three-layer hull is a full-dimensional
  convex body with exactly the asserted integer fibers A,B,A.
* The affine functional ell is measured in the original triangle's
  barycentric coordinate, including on the scaled endpoints. Hence
  A(t)=min(1/50,(1-t)_+^2) for every real t, not merely on [0,1].
* In the direct tilt optimization, a saturated endpoint cap contributes
  at least a; if neither saturates, convexity of the positive-part square
  gives the lower bound 2(1-t)_+^2. The two upper constructions attain
  the minimum, using tilt zero or a sufficiently large finite tilt.
  This includes every plateau, negative threshold, and threshold t=1.
* The derived tail is exactly the pushforward of 1_B+2 1_E, with
  E={ell>=9/10} intersect B. Its total is 51/50, as distinct from the
  original mixed total 26/25. The identification is a genuine measure
  identity and does not assume log-concavity.
* The means 1/3 and 14/15 give t_bar=88/255. At this threshold the
  normalized tail is 58379/132651, equal to the file's unreduced
  291895/663255. Its difference below gamma_2=4/9 is exactly
  577/132651>0.
* Closed boundaries have zero area in all relevant fibers. The note
  explicitly uses directional-capacity normalization and makes no OC
  assertion or claim that this derived law is the original mixed law.

No unproved optimization or limiting step remains in the construction.
